about.title: Carmel Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Carmel's mix of small galleries, restaurants, hospitality staff, and delivery and trade workers moving along Ocean Avenue, San Carlos Street, and Junipero Avenue means workplace injuries here often look different from a typical office claim. A server might slip on a wet floor, a delivery driver might get sideswiped near SR-1 (Cabrillo Highway), or a contractor might fall from scaffolding on a remodel. In California, workers' compensation is usually the exclusive route against your own employer no matter who was at fault, but if a negligent third party — a subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or another driver — contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim worth pursuing alongside your comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we're a free service that connects injured workers in Carmel with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims apply to your situation and what deadlines matter most.

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Picture
items.desc: Workers' compensation is generally the exclusive remedy against your employer, but if a subcontractor, property owner, or another driver caused your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible. An independent attorney can help identify whether that applies to your case.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim. Getting matched with an attorney early can help you understand what documentation and timing you need.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, But It Still Happens
items.desc: Employers cannot legally punish you for reporting an injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can advise you on your rights before you make any decisions.

items.question: I was hurt delivering packages near SR-1 in Carmel. Is this a workers' comp case or something else?
items.answer: It could be both. Workers' comp generally covers your medical costs and lost wages regardless of fault, but if another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate third-party injury claim against that driver. An independent attorney can look at the details and explain how the two claims interact.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: Generally, you should report the injury to your employer within 30 days to protect your workers' comp rights. If you're also pursuing a claim against a negligent third party, that claim typically carries a separate two-year deadline. It's worth getting guidance early so you don't lose either option.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim in Carmel?
items.answer: No — retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal in California. If you're concerned about how your employer might react, an independent attorney connected through LawProactive can walk you through your protections before you take any steps.
